title: Intake Air Temperature/Ambient Air Temperature Correlation
plain: After the car has sat long enough to cool down, the intake air temperature and outside air temperature readings should be close. The computer found that they disagree by too much.
symptoms: Usually no change in how the car drives
Outside temperature on the dash may look wrong

causes.name: Faulty intake air temperature sensor (often built into the MAF sensor)
Wiring or connector problem on either sensor
Car parked in strong sun or near a heat source, skewing one reading

checks: Compare both readings with a scan tool after the car sits overnight
Inspect both sensors and their connectors
fix: Usually replacing whichever sensor reads wrong, often the intake air temperature sensor or MAF sensor that contains it.

title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit/Open
plain: Some high-pressure fuel systems, mostly on diesels, use an electric valve to bleed off fuel pressure when needed. The computer found an open or broken connection in the circuit that controls this relief valve.
symptoms: Rough running, stalling or loss of power

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector at the relief valve
Failed fuel pressure relief valve solenoid

checks: Inspect the relief valve connector and wiring
Measure the solenoid resistance and compare to spec
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new fuel pressure relief valve.

title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit Low
plain: Some high-pressure fuel systems, mostly on diesels, use an electric valve to bleed off fuel pressure when needed. The computer found a voltage that is too low in the circuit that controls this relief valve.
symptoms: Rough running, stalling or loss of power

causes.name: Damaged wiring or loose connector at the relief valve
Failed fuel pressure relief valve solenoid

checks: Inspect the relief valve connector and wiring
Measure the solenoid resistance and compare to spec
fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new fuel pressure relief valve.

title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Circuit High
plain: Some high-pressure fuel systems, mostly on diesels, use an electric valve to bleed off fuel pressure when needed. The computer found a voltage that is too high in the circuit that controls this relief valve.

fix: Usually a wiring repair or a new fuel pressure relief valve.

title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Performance/Stuck Off
plain: The electric fuel pressure relief valve does not seem to open when the computer tells it to, so fuel pressure is not dropping the way it should.
symptoms: Rough running or stumbling when slowing down
checks: Watch commanded and actual rail pressure with a scan tool
Check the fuel for water or debris
fix: Usually a new fuel pressure relief valve, plus a fuel filter if the fuel is contaminated.

title: Fuel Pressure Relief Control Stuck On
plain: The electric fuel pressure relief valve appears to be stuck open, letting fuel pressure bleed away when it should be holding.

causes.name: Fuel pressure relief valve stuck open
Debris in the valve from contaminated fuel
Control circuit shorted so the valve stays on

checks: Watch rail pressure while cranking and running with a scan tool
Check the control wiring for a short
fix: Usually a new fuel pressure relief valve.

title: Charge Air Cooler Temperature Sensor Circuit (Bank 2)
plain: On turbocharged engines, the charge air cooler (intercooler) cools the boosted air. A sensor measures that air temperature, and the computer found a fault in the circuit from the bank 2 sensor.
checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare its reading with other temperature sensors after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new charge air temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

causes.name: Oil or soot fouling the sensor

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring
Compare its reading with other temperature sensors after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new charge air temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

checks: Inspect the sensor connector and wiring

title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Boost Control "A" Module Performance
plain: Some turbos use an electronic actuator with its own small control module to move the wastegate or variable vanes. The computer found that the "A" actuator module is not performing correctly.
symptoms: Loss of power or limp mode

causes.name: Failed electronic boost actuator or its module
Sticking wastegate or vane mechanism overloading the actuator
Power, ground or network wiring problem to the actuator

checks: Check for other actuator or network codes
Inspect the actuator wiring and connector
Run the actuator self-test or relearn with a scan tool
fix: Often a new electronic boost actuator, which sometimes comes only with the turbo. Check for a sticking mechanism first.

title: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit
plain: Some engines have a second coolant temperature sensor at the radiator outlet to help control the cooling fans and thermostat. The computer found a fault in the circuit from this sensor.
symptoms: Cooling fans may run all the time
Usually no change in engine temperature
checks: Check the coolant level
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring at the radiator
Compare its reading with the engine coolant temperature sensor after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new radiator coolant temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Radiator Coolant Temperature Sensor Circuit Range/Performance
plain: Some engines have a second coolant temperature sensor at the radiator outlet to help control the cooling fans and thermostat. The computer found a reading that does not make sense compared with other sensors from this sensor.
symptoms: Cooling fans may run all the time
Usually no change in engine temperature

causes.name: Thermostat stuck open or low coolant

checks: Check the coolant level
Inspect the sensor connector and wiring at the radiator
Compare its reading with the engine coolant temperature sensor after a cold soak
fix: Usually a new radiator coolant temperature sensor or a wiring repair.

title: Radiator Coolant Temperature/Engine Coolant Temperature Correlation
plain: After the engine has cooled down, the radiator coolant temperature and engine coolant temperature readings should be close. The computer found they disagree by too much.
symptoms: Cooling fans may run more than normal

causes.name: Low coolant or air in the cooling system

checks: Check the coolant level
Compare both readings after the car sits overnight
Watch both readings as the engine warms up
fix: Usually replacing whichever sensor reads wrong, or a thermostat if it is stuck open.

title: Engine Coolant Flow Low/Performance
plain: The computer has found that coolant is not flowing through the engine as well as it should. This can lead to overheating.
symptoms: Heater may blow cooler air than normal

causes.name: Low coolant level or air trapped in the system
Failing water pump, often an electric pump on newer engines
Stuck thermostat or coolant control valve

checks: Check the coolant level with the engine cold
Watch the temperature gauge; stop driving if it climbs toward hot
Have a shop test the water pump and thermostat
fix: Usually topping off and bleeding the coolant, or a new water pump or thermostat. Do not keep driving if the engine starts to overheat.

title: MAP - Mass or Volume Air Flow Correlation (Bank 2)
plain: The computer compares the manifold pressure sensor with the mass air flow sensor. Their readings for bank 2 do not agree, which usually means an air leak or a bad sensor.
checks: Look for cracked intake hoses and vacuum leaks
Clean or test the MAF sensor
Compare MAP and MAF readings with a scan tool
fix: Usually fixing an air leak or replacing the MAF or MAP sensor.

title: Low Pressure Fuel System Pressure - Too Low, Low Ambient Temperature
plain: In cold weather, the computer measured that the low-pressure fuel supply (from the tank pump) is lower than it should be.
symptoms: Hard starting or stalling in cold weather

causes.name: Diesel fuel gelling or waxing in the cold

checks: On diesels, make sure winter-blend fuel or an anti-gel additive is being used
Replace the fuel filter and drain any water
Check low-side fuel pressure with a gauge
fix: Often a new fuel filter and winter-grade fuel on diesels; otherwise a weak fuel pump.

title: Low Fuel Pressure - Forced Limited Power
plain: Fuel pressure has been too low for long enough that the computer has cut engine power to protect the engine.

causes.name: Weak fuel pump or high-pressure pump
Fuel leak or restricted fuel line

checks: Check for other fuel pressure codes
Replace the fuel filter if it is due
Check low-side and rail pressure with a gauge and scan tool
fix: Fix the cause of low fuel pressure, often a fuel filter or fuel pump.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly won't speed up or drops to idle, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Don't drive in traffic or on the highway until it's checked.

title: Fuel Injector Insufficient Flow - Forced Limited Power
plain: The computer has determined that the fuel injectors are not delivering enough fuel, so it has cut engine power to protect the engine.
checks: Check for low fuel pressure codes and fix those first
Have a shop run injector balance or flow tests
fix: Often fuel filter service and fuel system cleaning; worn injectors may need replacing.
urgent_if: If the car suddenly won't speed up or drops to idle, turn on your hazards, move right and get off the road when it's safe. Don't drive in traffic or on the highway until it's checked.

title: Mass or Volume Air Flow "A" Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too Low
plain: The mass air flow sensor measures how much air the engine takes in. The computer compared the "A" sensor reading with what it expected and found the measured air flow is too low.
symptoms: Possible reduced power or poor fuel economy

causes.name: Intake air leak after the MAF sensor
Clogged air filter or restricted intake

checks: Check the air filter and intake ducts
Clean the MAF sensor with MAF-safe cleaner
Compare MAF readings to expected values with a scan tool
fix: Often cleaning the MAF sensor or fixing an air leak; otherwise a new MAF sensor.

title: Mass or Volume Air Flow "A" Circuit Range/Performance - Air Flow Too High
plain: The mass air flow sensor measures how much air the engine takes in. The computer compared the "A" sensor reading with what it expected and found the measured air flow is too high.
symptoms: Possible reduced power or poor fuel economy

causes.name: Wrong or oiled aftermarket air filter fouling the sensor
Wiring problem at the MAF sensor

checks: Check the air filter and intake ducts
Clean the MAF sensor with MAF-safe cleaner
Compare MAF readings to expected values with a scan tool
fix: Often cleaning the MAF sensor or fixing an air leak; otherwise a new MAF sensor.
